newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT - Blue Square cut to hold.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Blue Square cut to hold.

text.p: UBS has dowgraded Blue Square Israel from a buy to a hold and cut its earnings per share (EPS) estimate for the Israeli retailer following a weaker than expected first quarter.
But UBS maintained its buy rating for its subsidiary Blue Square Chain Stores Properties & Investments, which trades in Tel Aviv.

Blue Square Israel has appreciated 75 percent since its initial public offering in New York last year. "This plus an earnings estimate reduction have brought the shares to fair value," UBS analyst Daniel Carasso wrote in a report released on Monday.
UBS lowered its EPS estimate for 1997 to 2.90 shekels from 3.55 and for 1998 to 3.50 from 4.20.
It also lowered its EPS estimate for Blue Square Chain Stores in 1997 to 2.45 shekels from 2.75 and in 1998 to 3.05 from 3.45.

Blue Square Chain Stores "still shows compelling valuation, despite a downward earnings revision and the circa 100 percent appreciation since we first rated the stock a buy in early 1996," the report said.
"On our new estimates Blue Square Chain Stores is currently trading at less than 16 times this year's and 13 times next year's earnings."
Blue Square Israel trades at about 22-23 times 1997 estimated earnings and 18-19 times 1998 estimated earnings.
